query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: By integrating high‐throughput DSC measurements with calibrated, third‐generation CALPHAD modeling, one can accurately and efficiently determine the melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change at melting, and liquid‐phase thermodynamic properties across a wide range of high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, single-phase high-entropy alloys (HEAs) in a well-characterized solid solution state
generation.intervention: Implement a high-throughput characterization protocol where each HEA specimen is subjected to DSC (and complementary dilatometry) measurements across the relevant temperature range, with the experimental data then calibrated and interpreted via an updated CALPHAD thermodynamic database that incorporates third-generation models for pure elements and Laves phases.
generation.conditions: DSC experiments conducted from room temperature to slightly above the solidus temperature under an inert atmosphere, using standardized reference materials for calibration; volume changes measured concurrently by dilatometry; CALPHAD calculations performed for the same temperature range with controlled input parameters to reflect the HEA’s composition.
generation.structural_mediator: The local chemical environment (ordering or distortions) in the HEAs moderates the enthalpy and entropy changes at melting and influences the liquid-phase density, which is captured indirectly by the DSC heat flow profiles and dilatometry data.
generation.mechanism: The DSC records endothermic peaks corresponding to melting, from which Tm, ∆Hm, and ∆Sm are deduced. Meanwhile, dilatometry detects volume changes upon melting. CALPHAD models, refined with high-quality pure-element data and known HEA phase boundaries, interpret these thermal signals and predict corresponding liquid-phase properties. The joint use of experiment and computation helps resolve subtle contributions of chemical substitutions that modify the thermodynamic parameters.
generation.predicted_outcome: The melting temperature will be determined with an accuracy comparable to established reference materials (i.e. within the typical error bounds for DSC), and the extracted fusion enthalpy and entropy, as well as volumetric changes, will quantitatively match the CALPHAD predictions within the expected uncertainty range. This performance is expected to hold for single-phase, as-cast HEAs within the compositional space where phase separation and strong crucible interactions are minimized.
generation.baseline: Traditional DSC measurements on neat materials and basic CALPHAD models that do not account for the subtleties of multicomponent interactions serve as the baseline.
generation.boundary: The approach applies to HEAs that are single-phase and exhibit clear DSC signals; it may be limited when phase changes, reactions with the crucible, or extreme compositional inhomogeneities are present.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainties arise from potential baseline drifts in DSC at high temperatures, subtle variations in ∆Hm and ∆Sm introduced by minor compositional deviations, and calibration challenges for dilatometry. Additionally, the accuracy of CALPHAD predictions depends on the reliability of the underlying thermodynamic database.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a representative library of HEAs spanning the intended compositional range and perform high-throughput DSC and dilatometry measurements under controlled, inert conditions. Independently calculate melting parameters using a third-generation CALPHAD database. Compare the experimental melting temperatures, fusion enthalpies, entropies, and volume changes with the CALPHAD-predicted values.
measurements: Dilatometry measurements for volume change at melting
CALPHAD-derived predictions of liquid-phase heat capacities and densities
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the DSC/dilatometry measurements systematically deviate from the CALPHAD predictions by more than the accepted combined uncertainty (i.e., if the experimental Tm, ∆Hm, ∆Sm, or volume change differ beyond expected error margins from independent reference methods), then the integrated DSC-CALPHAD approach is ruled out.

As shown in Fig. 4f1-f5 and g1-g5, after being written with DC voltages of +10 V and −10 V, respectively, read scans were performed every 4 min. It was observed that the polarization of BSCNT0.30 returned to its initial highly random state much faster compared to BSCNT0. Notably, as depicted in Fig. 4g5, BSCNT0.30 exhibited almost no identifiable PNRs after 12 min of polarized writing, highlighting the weak coupling between polar clusters. This suggests the presence of more dynamic PNRs in BSCNT0.30 ceramics, a significant characteristic of enhanced relaxation. The rapid reversibility of PNRs leads to reduced Pr, delayed polarization saturation, and ultimately exceptional energy storage performance. Given the advantage of excellent high-temperature resistance in dielectric ceramics, the temperature stability of their energy storage performance is of paramount importance.
